text: nNOS generates superoxide (·O2−) at low L-Arg; EPR spin-trapping in nNOS-transfected human kidney 293 cells showed the Ca2+ ionophore A23187 triggered NO without ·O2− in controls, whereas L-Arg-free medium produced ·O2− that increased as cytosolic L-Arg fell while NO declined. L-NAME abolished ·O2−. Nitrotyrosine accumulated in L-Arg-depleted cells; A23187 was cytotoxic there (marked LDH release), largely prevented by superoxide dismutase or L-NAME—peroxynitrite-mediated injury, so regulating arginine is a therapeutic target. p53 is activated by DNA damage (IR, radio-mimetic drugs, UV, MMS), hypoxia and nucleotide deprivation; kept low by its short half-life and weak DNA binding, activation raises its levels and DNA binding, inducing cell-cycle arrest, apoptosis or DNA repair via phosphorylation, dephosphorylation and acetylation of p53.
